content.text: Gallstones in the biliary tract (USU in the GB)
: ↑ in Asian pop, parasitic, bact infections
•OCPs (↑estrogen), Native Americans, bile stasis, chronic hemolysis, cirrhosis, infect, rapid wt loss, IBD, TPN, fibrates, ↑TG
▪︎also: DM, glucose intolerance, high carb intake, prolonged fasting >5d; meds: octreotide, ceftriaxone
Most are aSx – may be an incidental finding
nausea & precipitated by fatty foods or lrg meals
– initial TOC: stone in GB or cystic duct
: ursodeoxycholic acid may be used to dissolve the gallstones (takes 6-9mo); elective cholecystectomy
▪︎symptomatic: NSAIDs; pregnant pts w/ repeated symptomatic cholelithiasis or acute cholecystitis → lap cholecystectomy, preferably 2nd trimester
Porcelain gallbladder: partially/fully calcified GB on US — complication of chronic cholecystitis & RF for gallbladder CA

: low-carb or Mediterranean diet, physical activity, cardiorespiratory fitness; caffeinated coffee protective in women; fruits/vegetables/fiber → ↓ risk of cholecystectomy in women; Mg & poly-/monounsaturated fat protective in men
Inflam & infect of the GB ← obstruct of the cystic duct by gallstones
•fibrosis & thickening of the GB ← chronic inflam cell infiltration of the GB evident on histopathology –
precipitated by fatty foods or lrg meals
▪︎steady, severe & prolonged pain; may radiate to back; hx fatty food ≥1hr before onset; may have past milder/self-resolved episodes
▪︎ill appearing; lies still (motion → pain); RUQ tenderness w/ voluntary & involuntary guarding
: RUQ pain or inspir arrest w/ palpation of the GB
: referred pain to the Rt shoulder or subscapular area (phrenic n. irritate)
▪︎Boas sign: hyperesthesia/altered sensitivity below R scapula
: thickened or distended GB, pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy’s sign
CT scan: alt to U/S; can detect comp
▪︎CMP should be normal; ↑ total bili & alk phos → evaluate for biliary obstruct: cholangitis, choledocholithiasis, Mirizzi
: most accurate test – cholecystitis present if there = ⍉visualization of the GB

▪︎HIDA: tracer normally in CBD, GB & sm bowel w.in 30-60min; ⍉visualized by 60min → delayed imaging over several hrs or morphine augmentation; ⍉GB at 30min post morphine or on delayed images = diagnostic
▪︎MRCP if ↑ bili, ↑ transaminases, or bile duct dilate on U/S → r/o choledocholithiasis
▪︎Sx resolve 7-10d w/o tx but frequent severe comp → definitive tx indicated
▪︎admit: pain control, antiemetics, IVF, abx, NPO; abx until Sx resolve or GB removed (prevent sepsis & wound infect)
▪︎early lap chole w.in 7d of Sx onset = best risk ↓

▪︎acalculous or emphysematous cholecystitis → ↑ risk sepsis, gangrene, perforation (↑ mortality); surgery needed; percutaneous cholecystostomy may be initial for septic shock or comorbidities ⍉improving after 3d abx
← the presence of the stone blocking the bile duct
▪︎may be aSx; may also present w/ biliary pain or fever
▪︎suspect w/ ↑ bili, ↑ transaminases, or bile duct dilate on U/S
▪︎severe gallstone pancreatitis w/ jaundice or cholangitis → ERCP w/ sphincterotomy & stone extraction
biliary tract infect 2/2 obstruct of the CBD
diffuse fibrosis of intra/extrahepatic biliary ducts
